implementation_notes: A document is a data class and kotlinx.serialization is the codec: the @Serializable annotation makes the compiler plugin generate a serializer at compile time, Json.encodeToString(value) writes the document and Json.decodeFromString<T>(body) rebuilds it, with @SerialName pinning wire names and Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true } making a consumer tolerant of newer producers. Schemaless payloads use JsonElement/buildJsonObject instead of a generated serializer, and Jackson with the Kotlin module is the usual alternative when the rest of the stack already uses it. The data class plus generated serializer replaces the classic message class entirely; hand-written parsing survives only for fixed binary formats.
pitfalls: The compiler plugin has to be applied: without it @Serializable classes fail to compile rather than degrading to reflection.
ignoreUnknownKeys defaults to false, so a producer that adds a field makes strict consumers throw SerializationException; tolerance must be chosen per channel.
Sealed hierarchies need a registered class discriminator and that discriminator becomes part of the wire contract - renaming or moving a subclass stops old documents decoding.
Kotlin nullability is not on the wire: a non-null property missing from the document fails at decode time with a missing-field error.
